topic.title: @Transactional internals — proxies, propagation, rollback rules
topic.concept: Spring wraps the bean in a proxy that opens/commits the transaction around the method; the annotation does nothing when the call never crosses the proxy boundary.
points: Self-invocation bypasses the proxy — a @Transactional method calling another in the same class runs in the caller's transaction (or none).
Default rollback: unchecked exceptions only; checked exceptions commit unless rollbackFor is set.
REQUIRES_NEW suspends the outer transaction — a failure inside it does not roll back the caller.
JDK dynamic proxies need an interface; CGLIB subclasses the bean — final methods silently lose the aspect.
readOnly=true is a hint: Hibernate skips dirty checking; some drivers route to replicas.
topic.angle: 'Why did my @Transactional method not roll back?' — the classic trap. Strong answers check self-invocation, checked-exception defaults, and whether the proxy was even created.
